To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IMC PID rules can be simplified to a single tuning rule that is valid for first and second order plus time delay models, and that a simple rule exists to reduce the model order.

(a) the IMC PID controller tuning rules can be modified to improve disturbance response, and (b) simple analytic rules are available for model reduction that result in accurate first order or second-order plus time delay models.
the IMC PID controller tuning rules are simple and result in good closed-loop behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of PID controllers for industrial processes.
the development of simple rules for the design of controllers for industrial processes.
the design of a controller for a plant with a known transfer function, and the design is carried out in the frequency domain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rules presented here are a significant advance on previous rules for model reduction, PID controller tuning and the design of IMC controllers.
the rules are simple, robust, and effective.
the proposed analytic tuning rule is simple, easy to implement and gives excellent results for both setpoint tracking and disturbance rejection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the IMC PID rules are a good starting point, and that the modifications presented here improve performance for integrating processes and are simpler to use.
the PID tuning rules presented here are simple to apply, result in excellent closed loop behavior, and are easy to justify.
we have developed simple analytic rules for model identification, model reduction, and PID controller tuning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a single tuning rule that can be applied for all process models and that this rule can be applied directly to the process model obtained by model reduction.
simple analytic rules can be derived for model reduction and controller tuning that result in good closed-loop behavior.
there is no need for complicated tuning rules.
